text: A prince who succeeds to another of superior valour, may reign on by virtue of his predecessor's merits, and reap the fruits of his labours; but if he live to a great age, or if he be followed by another who is wanting in the qualities of the first, that then the kingdom must necessarily dwindle.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
